concepts.name: MatrixRTC Group Calls
concepts.summary: Element Call fork: decentralized video conferencing over the Matrix protocol (MatrixRTC, MSC4143) with LiveKit as the media backend (MSC4195). GroupCallView/InCallView drive the call lifecycle; the CallViewModel state layer keeps UI and RTC session in sync.

concepts.name: LiveKit Media Layer
concepts.summary: The SFU-facing side: openIDSFU.ts exchanges a Matrix OpenID token for a LiveKit access token, MatrixAudioRenderer plays remote tracks, and TrackProcessorContext/BlurBackgroundTransformer process local media before publishing.

concepts.name: End-to-End Encrypted Media
concepts.summary: Per-sender media encryption on top of the SFU: matrixKeyProvider distributes keys over Matrix, sharedKeyManagement covers password-protected rooms, e2eeAvailability gates the feature by platform support. Embedded widget sessions carry no Matrix crypto of their own.

concepts.name: Widget vs. Standalone Mode
concepts.summary: Two runtime modes: embedded as a Matrix-client widget (widget.ts, widget API messaging) or standalone SPA with its own Matrix session (matrixSessionStorage, auth/ login and passwordless registration).

concepts.name: Call Observability & Rageshake
concepts.summary: OpenTelemetry spans model the call (OTelCall, OTelGroupCallMembership, per-track media spans); rageshake uploads user bug reports with logs from the settings UI.

concepts.name: Local Dev Backend Stack
concepts.summary: backend/ ships a reproducible two-homeserver dev stack: Synapse configs, LiveKit configs, nginx and a local TLS CA — used to develop and test federation and calls locally.

flows.name: Joining a Group Call
flows.summary: User opens a call link or widget → GroupCallView resolves the Matrix room → openIDSFU exchanges the OpenID token for a LiveKit token → media tracks publish through the track processors → InCallView renders the grid; media E2EE keys arrive via matrixKeyProvider.

flows.name: Embedding as a Matrix Widget
flows.summary: A Matrix client embeds Element Call → widget.ts negotiates capabilities over the widget API → the host client supplies the session; no standalone Matrix login or crypto store is created in this mode.
